questions.question: A 65-year-old patient with a history of diabetes mellitus and coronary artery disease presents with dizziness and near syncope. ECG shows a wide-complex bradyarrhythmia. What is the most appropriate management?

Transcutaneous pacemaker insertion
Anticoagulant therapy with continuous observation
Atropine
questions.explanation: Symptomatic bradycardia with signs of poor perfusion (near-syncope) refractory to atropine requires transcutaneous pacing per ACLS bradycardia algorithm.

explanations.A: Amiodarone treats tachyarrhythmias, not symptomatic bradyarrhythmia; it can worsen bradycardia.
explanations.B: Symptomatic bradycardia with signs of poor perfusion (near-syncope) refractory to atropine requires transcutaneous pacing per ACLS bradycardia algorithm.
explanations.C: Anticoagulants do not correct the underlying rhythm problem; observation alone is unsafe in symptomatic bradycardia.
explanations.D: Atropine is first-line for symptomatic bradycardia but is ineffective in high-degree AV blocks with wide QRS; pacing is then indicated.
